sonnet.problem: The joke doesn't hold together. Leaving a batch with the timer ticking is an irresponsible act, while Jesus is commanding the right thing. The tag "so I'd go, but I'd go RUNNING" muddles the image. A stranger would say "huh?"
sonnet.rule: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it. ... A joke that doesn't make sense is worse than no joke.

sonnet.problem: The statement says an adversary "is taking you to court." Matthew 5:25 only says "while you are still on the way to court" and never says who takes the person there. The card adds an agent the text leaves open.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

sonnet.problem: Story card 12 already tells Jesus' rhetorical questions about tax collectors and Gentiles, which make the point of this question. The question then restates the same facts, so the earlier card gives away the answer ("nothing more than others already do").
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. ... Two lines that make the same point get one question.
